newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel slid against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in quiet trading, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today and the main activity was inter-bank trading. Most investors are sitting on the fence waiting to see the market's direction. Because of the low volume every deal moved the market," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The shekel fell because of the repayment of several dollar-linked loans. Today's movement is meaningless. The market can easily move in the other direction tomorrow," he said.
Dealers noted that until the central bank's interest rate announcement on Monday the market would remain volatile. The central bank's key lending rate is now at an annual 15.5 percent.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2800 shekels against 3.2510 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6691 shekels against 3.6394 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9073 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8844 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.1544 shekels against 2.1385 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2700 shekels.
